title: Printer Rate Became Per Printer Per Minute
text: id: COMP-005 domain: math title: Printer Rate Became Per Printer Per Minute tags: rates, printers, unit-rate memory: A printer problem became clear only when I found the per-printer-per-minute rate. Four printers and six minutes made a combined work window, not a single machine. I divided pages by printers and minutes, then rebuilt the new combined rate for the smaller printer group. I wrote the combined rate explicitly as printers times per-printer rate, with pages per minute beside it, before dividing pages by that rate. The final time carried minutes, not pages.

title: Printer Minutes Stayed In The Denominator
text: id: COMP-021 domain: math title: Printer Minutes Stayed In The Denominator tags: printers, rates, denominator, correction memory: I once divided pages by printers and accidentally called the result pages per minute. The missed denominator was time. The correction was pages divided by printers divided by minutes: 480 pages divided by 4 printers divided by 6 minutes gave 20 pages per printer per minute. Only after that did 3 printers become a 60 pages per minute combined rate. That mistake made me keep minutes in the denominator until the unit said pages per minute.
